verifications.claim: The Gospels document that God raised Jesus from the dead on the third day following his crucifixion.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 1 Corinthians 15:3–7 'raised on the third day'; Luke 24:46 'on the third day rise from the dead'; Mark 16:6 'He has risen'; R8: Luke 24:7 'on the third day be raised again'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple Gospel quotes in R3 and full Luke 24 in R8 directly document the resurrection on the third day.

verifications.claim: The resurrection of Jesus is celebrated on Easter.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Easter commemorates Jesus Christ's resurrection in Jerusalem and is celebrated by Christians as the foundation of their faith.'
verifications.reasoning: R2 explicitly states Easter celebrates the resurrection.

verifications.claim: Women followers, including Mary Magdalene, found the tomb empty on Sunday morning.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: Mark 16:1–8 'Mary Magdalene, Mary... first day of the week... stone rolled back... he is not here'; Matthew 28:1–10 'Mary Magdalene and the other Mary... first day'; R8: Luke 24:1-3 'women... first day of the week... stone rolled away... did not find the body'
verifications.reasoning: Direct quotes from Gospels in R3 and R8 confirm women including Mary Magdalene found empty tomb on first day (Sunday).

verifications.claim: The stone was rolled away from the tomb.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: Mark 16:4 'stone had been rolled back'; Matthew 28:2 'rolled back the stone'; R8: Luke 24:2 'stone rolled away from the tomb'
verifications.reasoning: Gospel quotes explicitly state the stone was rolled away.

verifications.claim: All four Gospels (Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John) detail the resurrection.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3 quotes resurrection accounts: Mark 16:1–8, Matthew 28:1–10, John 20:11–18, Luke 24:13–49
verifications.reasoning: R3 provides direct quotes from all four Gospels detailing resurrection events.

verifications.claim: The four Gospels note appearances of the risen Jesus to his disciples and others.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: John 20:11–18 Jesus to Mary; Matthew 28:9 Jesus met them; Luke 24 Jesus to Emmaus disciples and others; R8: Luke 24 appearances to Simon, Emmaus, disciples
verifications.reasoning: Quotes from Gospels in R3 and R8 show appearances in each Gospel.

verifications.claim: The accounts emphasize a bodily resurrection, not just a spiritual one.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3/R8: Luke 24:39 'a spirit does not have flesh and bones... Touch me'; R4: 'The bodily resurrection of Jesus Christ'
verifications.reasoning: Direct quotes and statements emphasize physical body, eating, touching.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3/R8: Luke 24:39-40 'See my hands and my feet... he showed them his hands and his feet'
verifications.reasoning: Luke 24 explicitly states Jesus showed hands and feet (wounds from crucifixion).

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3/R8: Luke 24:41-43 'Have you anything here to eat?... he took it and ate before them'
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote from Luke 24 confirms Jesus ate broiled fish.

verifications.claim: The Apostle Paul stated that if Christ was not raised, Christian faith is futile.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R3: 1 Corinthians 15:17 'if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile'
verifications.reasoning: Exact quote from Paul in 1 Corinthians 15.

verifications.claim: Jesus first appeared to Mary Magdalene outside the tomb.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R3: John 20:11–18 Mary first sees Jesus outside tomb; R8: Luke 24:34 'has appeared to Simon' before Emmaus report
verifications.reasoning: John supports Mary first; Luke implies Simon first, creating contradiction between sources.

verifications.claim: Jesus appeared to two disciples walking to Emmaus.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3/R8: Luke 24:13–49 'two of them were going to a village named Emmaus... Jesus himself drew near'
verifications.reasoning: Direct quotes from Luke 24 detail the Emmaus appearance.

verifications.claim: Jesus opened the Scriptures to the two disciples on the road to Emmaus.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3/R8: Luke 24:27 'he explained to them what was said in all the Scriptures'; 24:32 'opened to us the Scriptures'
verifications.reasoning: Luke 24 explicitly states Jesus opened/explained Scriptures to them.

verifications.claim: Jesus invited Thomas to touch his wounds to prove his physical resurrection.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No reference quotes or describes the Thomas incident specifically; R4 cites John 20:24-29 generally for appearances but no details on wounds or invitation.

verifications.claim: The risen Christ commanded his disciples to preach the gospel to all nations.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3/R8: Luke 24:47 'repentance for the forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed in his name to all nations'
verifications.reasoning: Luke 24 directly quotes the command to preach to all nations.
